items.title: AI拋售潮重創避險基金！十月股災致多頭崩潰、強平速度逾十年最快　巨額虧損引發裁員與策略收縮
items.title_en: AI Sell‑off Crushes Hedge Funds! October Market Crash Triggers Bull Collapse, Fastest Liquidations in Over a Decade, Massive Losses Lead to Layoffs and Strategy Cuts
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，10月股災重創避險基金，迫使它們以數年來最快的速度平倉，並透過裁員、削減投資策略控制風險。
《華爾街日報》報導，在周四(5日)美股拋售進一步加劇之前，許多基金已在上月蒙受巨額虧損並裁減人力，處於近年最痛苦階段。
從AI、醫療保健股票到高風險公司債，各類策略全線受創。根據摩根士丹利出具的最新研究報告，10月是選股型避險基金十餘年來最積極的平倉月份，市場部位自6月以來下降約9%。截至10月，超過40%的選股基金年內報酬為零或負值，儘管標普500與那斯達克指數全年仍維持正報酬。
高盛指出，科技、媒體、通訊類股基金週四(5日)一天虧逾4%，幾乎抹平今年一度高達24%的漲幅；跨資產多策略基金也因科技與動量交易失利下跌1.4%。
跌勢源於「AI多頭交易」的集中逆轉。民主黨確定掌控國會兩院後，市場擔心AI基建與資料中心監管收緊，資金迅速從高風險科技倉位撤出，轉進美債與防禦型股票。
管理約70億美元的Samlyn Capital今年前十月虧損約5%，正把重心縮小至金融股交易，並有多名行業負責人與投資團隊離職。
Glenn Dubin創辦的Engineers Gate近期解散大部分「量質混合(quantamental)」策略，相關投資組合經理僅留任5人，業務負責人Mike Daylamani去職。
Lone Pine Capital今年上半年曾大賺逾40%，但第三季遭遇史上最差季度表現，10月再跌8.8%，年內轉為虧損7.5%；該避險基金業者在AI多頭與「反AI受惠股」的錯向押注雙雙失利。
Walleye Capital在上月經歷2020年3月以來最差月度表現後，本周裁員多位選股經理，並打算退還部分客戶資金，昔日高歌猛進的Arini Capital則因銀行追繳保證金，近期大舉削減債券持倉。
為控管風險，避險基因業者近幾週持續砍團隊、平倉、降槓桿。一位主管表示，若非前期已削減借貸放大部位，週四虧損會更難看。
當前困境在於：多策略基金慣用的宏觀、固收、動量等風格同步失效，擁擠交易反噬自身，越是共同減倉，越壓垮持倉價格。美債殖利率、美伊戰情與AI監管節奏是市場關注的下一個變數，任何一項反轉都可能決定這波平倉潮是暫時止血，還是演變成新一輪去槓桿風暴。
paras_en: Foreign media reports say the October market crash hit hedge funds hard, forcing them to unwind positions at the fastest pace in years and to cut staff and investment strategies to manage risk.

The Wall Street Journal reported that before the U.S. stock sell‑off intensified on Thursday (the 5th), many funds had already suffered huge losses last month and were trimming headcount, entering their most painful period in recent years.

From AI and healthcare stocks to high‑yield corporate bonds, every strategy was hit. Morgan Stanley’s latest research shows October was the most aggressive unwind month for stock‑picking hedge funds in more than a decade, with market exposure down about 9% since June. By the end of October, over 40% of stock‑picking funds had zero or negative returns year‑to‑date, even though the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted positive returns for the year.

Goldman Sachs noted that technology, media and communications funds lost more than 4% on Thursday (the 5th), erasing almost all of the year‑to‑date 24% gain; cross‑asset multi‑strategy funds also fell 1.4% after tech and momentum trades went sour.

The decline stemmed from a sharp reversal of “AI‑long” trades. After Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, markets feared tighter regulation of AI infrastructure and data centers, prompting a rapid pull‑back from high‑risk tech positions into U.S. Treasuries and defensive stocks.

Samlyn Capital, which manages about $7 billion, lost roughly 5% in its first ten months of the year and is now narrowing its focus to financial‑sector trading, with several senior industry heads and investment team members departing.
Engineers Gate, founded by Glenn Dubin, recently dismantled most of its “quantamental” strategies, leaving only five portfolio managers, and its business head Mike Daylamani has left the firm.

Lone Pine Capital posted a more than 40% gain in the first half of the year but suffered its worst quarterly performance ever in Q3 and fell another 8.8% in October, turning a 7.5% year‑to‑date loss after its AI‑long and “anti‑AI beneficiary” bets both went wrong.

After posting its worst monthly performance since March 2020, Walleye Capital this week laid off several stock‑picking managers and plans to return some client capital; the once‑high‑flying Arini Capital is slashing bond holdings after banks demanded margin calls.

To manage risk, hedge‑fund operators have been cutting teams, unwinding positions and lowering leverage in recent weeks. One senior manager said that if they hadn’t already trimmed leveraged exposure, Thursday’s losses would have been even worse.

The current dilemma is that the macro, fixed‑income and momentum styles that multi‑strategy funds rely on have all faltered simultaneously, with crowded trades back‑firing. The more everyone reduces exposure, the more it depresses prices. U.S. Treasury yields, the Israel‑Iran conflict and the pace of AI regulation are the next variables on market participants’ radar, and any reversal could determine whether this wave of liquidations is a temporary stop‑gap or the start of a new de‑leveraging storm.

items.title: 輝達暴跌逾9%跌入熊市！基金經理人：買點來了
items.title_en: Nvidia Plummets Over 9% Into Bear Market! Fund Managers Say Buying Opportunity Arrives
paras: 輝達 (NVDA-US) 週四 (5 日) 暴跌 9.26%，收在 181.60 美元，較 10 月歷史收盤高點回落約 24.1%，正式跌入熊市。美國期中選舉後，市場擔憂資料中心建設將面臨更多政治阻力，引爆人工智慧 (AI) 晶片股賣壓。不過，部分基金經理人認為，AI 晶片需求與輝達競爭優勢仍具支撐，股價急跌可能帶來買進機會。
輝達週四創下 2025 年 1 月 DeepSeek 引發科技股拋售以來最大單日跌幅，單日市值蒸發約 4,470 億美元，為歷來第二大單日市值損失。自 10 月 6 日創下歷史收盤新高以來，累計市值縮水近 1.4 兆美元，目前約為 4.4 兆美元。
這波賣壓也使輝達跌破 200 日移動均線。截至週四，股價本週累計下跌約 11%，朝連續第五週收黑邁進，顯示投資人對 AI 產業前景的疑慮，已持續反映在股價上。
此次拋售的核心壓力來自華府。
民主黨在期中選舉奪回參眾兩院控制權，加上兩黨部分候選人選前均曾反對資料中心擴建，使市場擔心，供電成本與地方建設爭議將轉化為更嚴格的政策限制。
美國參議院今年秋季曾接近通過一項法案，要求資料中心承擔更多自身需求所衍生的電力成本。
對晶片業而言，市場關注的傳導風險在於，一旦資料中心建設延宕或成本提高，雲端業者部署 AI 運算設備的速度可能放慢，進而影響晶片採購時程。
Stifel 分析師 Brian Gardner 期中選舉前表示，國會將出現聽證會與調查。這也意味著，投資人除了評估 AI 需求與企業支出，還必須將政治監督對建設進度的影響納入考量。
然而，Founder ETFs 投資組合經理人Michael Monaghan 認為，市場短線波動不完全反映基本面變化，高槓桿交易與風險控管也放大了跌勢。
他指出，部分避險基金使用高槓桿操作，同時受到嚴格風險限額約束，當股價開始下跌，就必須迅速減碼，使盤中跌幅進一步擴大。不過，相同的交易結構也可能讓市場在情緒改善時快速反彈。
Monaghan 預期，輝達明年營收可望成長約 70%。他認為，即使市場擔憂資料中心建設受阻，相關工程仍可能持續推進，支撐 AI 晶片需求，因此在本月稍晚財報公布前，這波跌勢已浮現布局機會。
他也看好新一代 Rubin 晶片帶來的業務動能，並以 SpaceX 近期與阿波羅全球管理 (Apollo Global Management) 達成的 400 億美元融資協議為例，指出大型企業仍在籌措資金取得 AI 晶片。
在他看來，AI 支出與需求的基本面尚未遭到破壞，當股價走勢與基本面背離，往往會形成具吸引力的投資機會。
Aptus Capital Advisors 投資組合經理人 David Wagner 則指出，輝達估值下修，反映投資人擔心其獲利高度依賴龐大的 AI 基礎建設支出，而這些支出未來可能放緩。
不過，他認為，輝達的優勢不僅來自晶片效能，也包括軟體生態系，以及圍繞其平台建立應用的開發者群體。這些條件使輝達可能擁有 AI 產業中最深厚的護城河。
因此，若投資人仍相信 AI 建設將延續多年，週四跌勢更接近估值重新調整，尚不足以推翻長期投資論點。
歷史表現則提醒投資人，連跌本身並不保證反彈。數據統計顯示，自 1999 年上市以來，輝達此前僅出現過 12 次至少連跌五週的情況，其中只有五次在 13 週後上漲，八次在一年後上漲。
最近一次類似跌勢於 2022 年 10 月結束，之後一年輝達股價漲至約四倍，受惠於 ChatGPT 問世帶動 AI 熱潮；但在 2002 年的案例中，股價於隨後一年再跌近三分之二，顯示後續表現仍取決於產業與獲利走勢。
對看多輝達的基金經理人而言，這波急跌提供了以較低價格參與長期 AI 成長的機會；但買點能否成立，仍有賴資料中心建設持續推進，以及晶片訂單順利轉化為營收。本月稍晚公布的財報與管理層展望，將成為市場檢驗政策疑慮是否已影響實際需求的重要依據。
paras_en: Nvidia (NVDA-US) tumbled 9.26% on Thursday (the 5th), closing at $181.60, about 24.1% below its October historical high and officially entering bear market territory. After the U.S. midterm elections, the market feared data‑center construction would face greater political resistance, sparking sell‑offs in AI chip stocks. Yet some fund managers argue that AI chip demand and Nvidia’s competitive edge remain supportive, and the sharp drop could present a buying chance.

Nvidia recorded its biggest single‑day decline since the DeepSeek‑driven tech sell‑off in January 2025, erasing roughly $447 billion of market value in one day – the second‑largest one‑day loss on record. Since hitting a new historical closing high on October 6, its market cap has shrunk by nearly $1.4 trillion and now sits around $4.4 trillion.

The sell‑off also pushed Nvidia below its 200‑day moving average. By Thursday, the stock had fallen about 11% for the week, heading toward a fifth consecutive week of losses, reflecting investors’ lingering doubts about the AI sector’s outlook.
The core pressure behind this sell‑off originates from Washington.

Democrats reclaimed control of both chambers of Congress in the midterms, and several candidates from both parties had previously opposed data‑center expansion, prompting market worries that higher power costs and local construction disputes could translate into stricter policy limits.
The U.S. Senate this fall came close to passing a bill that would require data centers to shoulder more of the electricity costs they generate.

For the chip industry, the market’s concern is the transmission risk: if data‑center builds are delayed or become more expensive, cloud providers may slow the deployment of AI compute equipment, which would in turn push back chip procurement schedules.

Stifel analyst Brian Gardner warned before the midterms that Congress would hold hearings and investigations. That means investors must factor not only AI demand and corporate spending but also the impact of political oversight on construction timelines.

However, Founder ETFs portfolio manager Michael Monaghan believes the market’s short‑term volatility does not fully reflect fundamental changes, and that high‑leverage trading and risk controls have amplified the decline.

He notes that some hedge funds use high‑leverage strategies while being bound by strict risk limits; when the price starts falling they must quickly unwind positions, widening intraday drops. Yet the same structure can also enable a rapid rebound if sentiment improves.

Monaghan expects Nvidia’s revenue to grow about 70% next year. He thinks that even if data‑center construction faces obstacles, related projects are likely to keep moving forward, sustaining AI chip demand, so the current slide before this month’s earnings release already offers a positioning opportunity.

He is also bullish on the next‑generation Rubin chip’s business momentum, citing SpaceX’s recent $40 billion financing deal with Apollo Global Management as an example that large firms are still raising capital to acquire AI chips.
In his view, the fundamentals of AI spending and demand have not been damaged; when price action diverges from fundamentals, attractive investment opportunities often emerge.

Aptus Capital Advisors portfolio manager David Wagner points out that Nvidia’s valuation downgrade reflects investor worries that its profits are heavily dependent on massive AI infrastructure spending, which could slow in the future.

Nevertheless, he argues that Nvidia’s advantage lies not only in chip performance but also in its software ecosystem and the developer community building applications around its platform, giving it perhaps the deepest moat in the AI industry.
Thus, if investors still believe AI infrastructure will continue for years, Thursday’s drop is more a valuation adjustment than a reason to overturn a long‑term investment thesis.

Historical data remind investors that a string of declines does not guarantee a rebound. Since its IPO in 1999, Nvidia has only experienced 12 instances of at least five consecutive weeks of decline, and only five of those saw a rise after 13 weeks, while eight recovered within a year.

The most recent similar decline ended in October 2022; a year later Nvidia’s stock had risen roughly fourfold, fueled by the AI boom sparked by ChatGPT. By contrast, the 2002 case saw the price fall nearly two‑thirds in the following year, showing that subsequent performance depends on industry and earnings trends.

For bullish fund managers, this sharp drop offers a chance to participate in long‑term AI growth at a lower price; however, whether the buying point holds depends on continued data‑center construction and chip orders translating into revenue. The upcoming earnings report and management outlook later this month will be key gauges of whether policy concerns have already impacted actual demand.

items.title: 砸重金德州仍變天 馬斯克AI擴張添變數、SpaceX合約恐迎國會檢視
items.title_en: Heavy Spending Fails to Keep Texas Red; Musk's AI Expansion Faces New Variables, SpaceX Contracts May Face Congressional Scrutiny
paras: 民主黨在美國期中選舉拿下德州州長與聯邦參議員席次，並時隔23年重掌州眾議院，讓馬斯克商業帝國的重要據點面臨政策變數。
從資料中心許可、電力供應到租稅優惠，當地投資環境可能調整；隨著民主黨掌控國會兩院，旗下企業的政府合約與AI業務，也面臨更嚴格監督的可能。
德州政策轉向 AI擴張添變數
德州長期以低監管、相對充裕的能源及親商環境吸引科技企業，也是馬斯克布局重鎮。特斯拉在當地設有重要生產基地，SpaceX星際基地位於德州南部，旗下企業也計劃在當地推進晶片製造業務。
不過，民主黨新當選州長希諾霍薩對資料中心建設態度審慎。她在競選期間承諾，在州議會制定保護社區、居民電價、水資源與產權的法律前，暫停核發新的資料中心建設許可，並重新檢視相關租稅優惠。
她主張，企業應承擔電力與基礎建設費用，不能讓居民生活成本因資料中心發展而增加。
這項政策方向，可能牽動馬斯克旗下企業的AI布局。xAI資料中心擴張需要大量電力，SpaceX也將AI運算視為未來業務的重要組成部分。若審核收緊、優惠調整，相關建設時程與資本支出安排都可能受到影響。
據路透社報導，德州選舉結果公布後，市場開始重新評估馬斯克旗下企業的政策風險。分析師指出，SpaceX先前向投資人展示的商業前景包含大規模AI運算業務，資料中心核准放緩，可能影響相關擴張計畫。
用電需求龐大 建設未必全面停擺
德州是美國AI資料中心擴張重鎮。德州電力可靠性委員會（ERCOT）數據顯示，大型用電計畫的電網併網申請規模一度達約474吉瓦，其中約90%來自資料中心，超過電網歷史尖峰負載的五倍。
報導指出，德州約占美國規劃新增資料中心容量的四分之一，政策變化可能波及全美AI基礎建設。
但這不代表資料中心將全面停建。今年8月，現任州長阿博特下令暫停新的電網接入後，Meta(META-US) 、微軟(MSFT-US) 、OpenAI、亞馬遜(AMZN-US) 雲端服務等至少43家企業公開支持相關審查。企業支持審查，並不等於支持無限期停建，重點仍是審批規則能否明確、計畫能否如期推進。
2027年1月新一屆州議會開議後，資料中心立法可能成為重要議題。電網擴充成本如何分攤、資源使用資訊揭露、地方社區參與權及租稅優惠是否延續，都可能影響投資成本與建設週期。
國會監督升溫 SpaceX合約受關注
馬斯克的政策壓力也延伸至聯邦層級。民主黨贏得國會兩院後，新國會預料將加強監督大型科技企業及其政府業務。
馬斯克先前在「政府效率部」（DOGE）推動的聯邦裁員、SpaceX取得的政府合約與補貼，以及衛星通訊服務在烏克蘭軍事行動中的使用，都可能成為議員檢視的議題。
SpaceX長期承接美國政府航太發射與國防業務，政府合約是其商業版圖的重要部分。這些合約短期內不易被替代，但國會監督、預算審查及採購政策變化，仍可能影響未來合約審批與執行。
此外，民主黨議員先前主張強化AI安全、資料透明度與科技企業責任，相關立法及監管討論可能進一步推進。不過，政策方向改變不等於企業立即受到新限制，實際影響仍取決於後續程序。
豪擲政治獻金 未換來預期勝局
馬斯克此次大舉投入資金支持共和黨。《華盛頓郵報》依競選財務申報統計，他在2026年期中選舉週期個人投入約4.46億美元，創美國現代政治史個人政治捐款紀錄。
據《德州論壇報》報導，馬斯克透過共和黨參議院主要超級政治行動委員會等管道，向候選人帕克斯頓提供近1.9億美元支持。然而，截至11月4日，他支持的多名候選人已確定落敗。
分析指出，德州選舉失利不代表金錢失去政治影響力，卻顯示競選資金無法直接決定選票。對馬斯克而言，政治影響力與商業利益的深度綁定，也可能在地方與聯邦政治轉向時，成為企業政策風險的來源。
paras_en: Democrats won the Texas governor’s seat and a U.S. Senate seat in the midterm elections, and after a 23‑year gap reclaimed the state House, creating policy uncertainties for key outposts of Elon Musk’s business empire.

From data‑center permits and power supply to tax incentives, the local investment climate could shift; with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress, the government contracts and AI operations of Musk’s companies may also come under tighter oversight.
Texas policy shift adds variables to AI expansion

Texas has long attracted tech firms with low regulation, relatively abundant energy and a pro‑business environment, making it a cornerstone of Musk’s strategy. Tesla has a major manufacturing base there, SpaceX’s Starbase is in South Texas, and his affiliates plan to advance chip‑making activities in the state.

However, newly elected Democratic Governor Cindy Hinohosha takes a cautious stance on data‑center construction. During her campaign she pledged to pause the issuance of new data‑center permits until the state legislature enacts laws protecting communities, resident electricity rates, water resources and property rights, and to re‑examine related tax breaks.
She argues that companies should bear the costs of power and infrastructure and should not let residents’ living expenses rise because of data‑center development.

This policy direction could affect the AI rollout of Musk’s companies. xAI’s data‑center expansion requires massive electricity, and SpaceX also views AI computing as a key future business component. If approvals tighten and incentives change, construction timelines and capital‑expenditure plans could be impacted.

According to Reuters, after the Texas election results were announced, markets began reassessing the policy risk for Musk’s firms. Analysts noted that SpaceX’s previously presented commercial outlook included large‑scale AI computing services, and a slowdown in data‑center approvals could affect those expansion plans.
Huge power demand means construction may not halt entirely

Texas is a major hub for AI data‑center expansion in the United States. Data from the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) shows that applications to connect large‑scale power projects once reached about 474 GW, roughly 90 % of which came from data‑centers, more than five times the grid’s historic peak load.
The report points out that Texas accounts for about a quarter of the new data‑center capacity planned nationwide, so policy changes could ripple through AI infrastructure across the country.

But this does not mean data‑centers will stop being built altogether. In August, incumbent Governor Greg Abbott ordered a pause on new grid connections, after which at least 43 companies—including Meta (META‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US), OpenAI and Amazon (AMZN‑US) cloud services—publicly supported the review. Corporate backing of the review does not equate to support for an indefinite construction freeze; the key issue remains whether approval rules are clear and projects can proceed as scheduled.

When the new state legislature convenes in January 2027, data‑center legislation is likely to become a major topic. How grid‑expansion costs are shared, disclosure of resource‑use information, local community participation rights and the continuation of tax incentives could all affect investment costs and construction timelines.
Congressional oversight heats up, SpaceX contracts draw attention

Musk’s policy pressures also extend to the federal level. With Democrats winning control of both chambers, the new Congress is expected to tighten supervision of large tech firms and their government business.

Musk’s earlier efforts in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) to cut federal staffing, the government contracts and subsidies SpaceX has secured, and the use of its satellite communications in Ukraine’s military operations could all become subjects of congressional review.

SpaceX has long handled U.S. government aerospace launch and defense contracts, which are a significant part of its commercial portfolio. These contracts are not easily replaceable in the short term, but congressional oversight, budget reviews and changes to procurement policy could still affect future contract approvals and execution.

In addition, Democratic lawmakers have previously advocated strengthening AI safety, data transparency and tech‑company accountability. Related legislation and regulatory discussions may advance further. However, a shift in policy direction does not instantly impose new restrictions on companies; the actual impact will depend on subsequent procedures.
Huge political donations did not yield the expected victory

Musk poured a massive amount of money into supporting Republicans this time. According to the Washington Post’s campaign‑finance filings, he personally contributed about $446 million during the 2026 midterm election cycle, setting a modern‑American record for individual political donations.

The Texas Tribune reported that Musk, through major Republican Senate super‑PACs and other channels, gave nearly $190 million in support to candidate Parker Stone. Yet, as of November 4, several of the candidates he backed have already been confirmed as losers.

Analysts note that the Texas defeat does not mean money has lost political influence, but it shows that campaign funds cannot directly decide votes. For Musk, the deep intertwining of political influence and business interests could become a source of policy risk for his enterprises as state and federal politics shift.

items.title: 美國反AI勢力不會讓需求消失 留給產業更多時間吸收泡沫
items.title_en: US anti‑AI forces won’t make demand disappear, giving the industry more time to absorb the bubble
paras: 美國國會期中選舉的結果，正在給人工智慧（AI）產業帶來一個意想不到的變量。美國民主黨在多個關鍵州取得勝利，部分候選人承諾暫停或收緊資料中心建設審批。
反資料中心勢力悄然崛起，市場開始擔憂美國AI基礎設施擴張遭遇阻力，全球晶片股巨震，三星電子、SK海力士等企業面臨伺服器DRAM和高頻寬記憶體需求預期變化的風險。
但科技作者Derek Thompson提出了一個反直覺的觀點：美國日益激烈的反AI政治，短期可能打壓AI股票，卻有望在中長期幫助整個產業避免泡沫。
Thompson曾在美國《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）擔任專職撰稿人長達17年，長期關注科技、經濟、勞動力市場與社會趨勢，也是暢銷書《豐裕》（Abundance）合著者，目前主持播客《Plain English》。
這一判斷的關鍵，不在於反AI運動會讓AI需求消失，而在於它可能改變AI供給擴張的速度。歷史上科技泡沫往往伴隨著基礎設施投資跑在真實需求前面。
如果政治阻力放慢資料中心建設，讓需求有時間追上供給，反AI運動反而可能無意中為AI產業踩下剎車。
美國期中選舉後，資料中心的政治風險開始受到市場關注。
民主黨在德州等關鍵州取得勝利，部分候選人明確提出對新資料中心祭出暫停令。德州尤其引人關注，據GLJ Research估計，德州約佔美國至2030年計畫投入使用的資料中心容量的四分之一。
喬治亞州同樣是重要資料中心市場。CBRE的數據顯示，亞特蘭大是全美在建資料中心規模最活躍的市場之一。民主黨Keisha Lance Bottoms贏得州長選舉，也讓市場開始評估當地資料中心建設政策可能面臨的變化。
反資料中心情緒並非單純黨派衝突。當地居民反對項目，主要擔憂噪音、耗水、巨大電力需求，以及資料心建設可能推高居民電費。
與此同時，社區也質疑資料中心創造的就業崗位和稅收貢獻，是否足以匹配政府提供的獎勵政策。
這種牴觸情緒正在跨越黨派界限。隨著資料中心擴張與地方電力、土地和水資源矛盾日益突出，AI基礎設施建設不再只是科技企業與投資者的商業決策，也開始成為地方政治議題。
市場擔憂由此而來：如果更多州採取暫停令或提高審批門檻，美國資料中心擴張速度可能放緩，進而影響伺服器、記憶體晶片、高頻寬記憶體等AI基礎設施供應鏈的需求預期。
paras_en: The results of the US midterm elections are introducing an unexpected variable for the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. The Democratic Party won in several key states, and some candidates have pledged to pause or tighten approvals for data‑center construction.

An anti‑data‑center movement is quietly emerging, prompting market concerns that US AI infrastructure expansion could face resistance. Global chip stocks have been jolted, with companies like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix facing risk from changing expectations for server DRAM and high‑bandwidth memory demand.

But technology writer Derek Thompson offers a counter‑intuitive view: the increasingly intense anti‑AI politics in the US may depress AI stocks in the short term but could help the whole industry avoid a bubble in the medium to long term.

Thompson spent 17 years as a full‑time writer for The Atlantic, focusing on technology, economics, the labor market and social trends, and co‑authored the bestseller Abundance. He now hosts the podcast Plain English.

The key to his judgment is not that the anti‑AI movement will eliminate AI demand, but that it could slow the pace of AI supply expansion. Historically, tech bubbles often featured infrastructure investment outpacing real demand.
If political resistance slows data‑center construction, giving demand time to catch up with supply, the anti‑AI movement may unintentionally apply the brakes to the AI industry.
After the US midterms, the political risk to data‑centers has begun to attract market attention.

Democrats won in key states such as Texas, where some candidates have explicitly called for a pause on new data‑centers. Texas is especially noteworthy; GLJ Research estimates it will account for about a quarter of the data‑center capacity slated for operation in the US by 2030.

Georgia is also an important data‑center market. CBRE data shows Atlanta is one of the most active markets for data‑center construction in the country. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms’ victory in the governor’s race has led the market to assess possible policy shifts for local data‑center projects.

The anti‑data‑center sentiment is not merely a partisan clash. Local residents oppose projects mainly due to concerns about noise, water consumption, massive electricity demand, and the potential for data‑centers to raise residential power bills.
At the same time, communities question whether the jobs and tax revenues generated by data‑centers are sufficient to justify the incentives offered by governments.

This opposing sentiment is crossing party lines. As data‑center expansion increasingly clashes with local electricity, land and water resources, AI infrastructure construction is no longer just a commercial decision for tech firms and investors but is becoming a local political issue.

The market worries that if more states impose pause orders or raise approval thresholds, the pace of US data‑center expansion could slow, affecting demand forecasts for servers, memory chips, high‑bandwidth memory and other AI infrastructure supply‑chain components.

items.title: 美科技股血洗引發避險潮！全美貨幣基金成資金避風港　規模突破8兆美元
items.title_en: US Tech Stock Bloodbath Sparks Hedge Wave! Money‑Market Funds Become Safe‑Haven Across the US, Size Tops $8 Trillion
paras: 美股拋售潮持續擴大，投資人加速撤離風險資產，資金轉進美債與貨幣市場基金。隨著AI概念股遭遇大規模賣壓，短天期美債成為首選避險標的，兩年期美債殖利率週四(5日)重挫近11個基點至約4.48%，創今年9月9日以來新低。
美股週四全面重挫，那斯達克收跌5.52%、那斯達克100指數跌6.36%，雙雙進入技術性回調階段；標普500跌4.36%，道瓊跌3.44%，費城半導體指數更暴跌12.25%。
威靈頓管理固定收益經理Brij Khurana指出，市場正大量買入短債，並開始為股市進一步下跌的尾部風險定價。
宏利投資管理利率交易主管Mike Lorizio認為，美債正重新發揮避險功能。
不過，長債反應相對溫和，10年期美債殖利率僅下跌約5個基點，顯示資金主要反映短期市場震盪，尚未完全押注長期衰退。
另據美國投資公司協會(ICI)數據顯示，貨幣市場基金資產規模攀至8.016兆美元歷史新高，反映大量資金暫離風險資產、等待局勢明朗，但此數字為基金總規模，不代表單日有等量資金從股市撤出。
拋售核心在於AI基建敘事面臨重估。民主黨全面贏得國會主導權後，市場擔憂新國會與部分州政府將加強AI資料中心監管，電力、水資源與環保爭議可能拖慢AI資本支出。
分析師認為，支撐半導體與科技股市值的「AI軍備競賽」邏輯若放緩，增長預期將面臨修正，並可能沿著財富效應傳導至消費與實體經濟。
股市劇烈波動也改變Fed路徑預期。芝商所FedWatch顯示，市場押注12月升息機率由82.7%降至66.1%，明年3月前累計升息幅度預期同步下調。
但瑞銀固定收益策略主管Leslie Falconio仍預期12月與明年3月各升息一次，但認為緊縮空間有限，AI建設不會全面停擺，只是推進速度將放緩。
接下來市場焦點轉向週五(6日)出爐的10月非農就業報告。Khurana指出，若數據強於預期，對股市的負面衝擊恐大於債市。在政策與政治不確定性交織下，資金防禦姿態短期難解。
paras_en: The sell‑off in US equities kept widening as investors accelerated the exit from risk assets and shifted cash into US Treasuries and money‑market funds. With AI‑related stocks under massive selling pressure, short‑term US bonds became the preferred safe‑haven, and the two‑year Treasury yield plunged nearly 11 basis points on Thursday (the 5th) to about 4.48%, a low not seen since September 9 this year.

US stocks fell across the board on Thursday: the Nasdaq dropped 5.52%, the Nasdaq‑100 fell 6.36%, both entering technical correction territory; the S&P 500 slipped 4.36%, the Dow Jones fell 3.44%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25%.
Brij Khurana, a fixed‑income manager at Wellington Management, noted that the market is buying short‑dated bonds in large volumes and beginning to price in tail‑risk from further equity declines.
Mike Lorizio, head of rates trading at Manulife Investment Management, said US Treasuries are once again serving their traditional safe‑haven role.

However, long‑dated bonds reacted more modestly, with the 10‑year Treasury yield down only about five basis points, indicating that capital is mainly responding to short‑term market turbulence and has not yet fully bet on a prolonged recession.

Data from the Investment Company Institute (ICI) show that assets in money‑market funds have climbed to a historic $8.016 trillion, reflecting a large flow of cash away from risk assets as investors wait for clarity. The figure represents total fund assets and does not imply that an equivalent amount was withdrawn from equities in a single day.

The core of the sell‑off lies in a reassessment of the AI‑infrastructure narrative. After Democrats secured full control of Congress, markets worry that the new Congress and some state governments will tighten regulation of AI data centers, with power, water and environmental disputes potentially slowing AI capital spending.

Analysts argue that if the "AI arms race" logic that underpins semiconductor and tech valuations slows, growth expectations will be revised downward and could transmit through wealth effects to consumer spending and the real economy.

The sharp market swings also altered expectations for the Fed’s policy path. CME FedWatch showed the probability of a December rate hike falling from 82.7% to 66.1%, and expectations for the cumulative rate hikes before March next year were trimmed accordingly.

Nevertheless, Leslie Falconio, head of fixed‑income strategy at UBS, still expects one rate hike in December and another in March, but believes the room for tightening is limited and AI construction will not come to a complete halt—just a slower pace.

The market’s next focus shifts to Friday’s (the 6th) October non‑farm payroll report. Khurana warned that if the data beat expectations, the negative impact on equities could be larger than on bonds. With policy and political uncertainty intertwined, defensive positioning of capital will remain difficult to unwind in the short term.

items.title: 晶片股殺到甜甜價？《巴隆》點名買入台積電等五檔優質股
items.title_en: Chip Stocks Plunge to Sweet Prices? "Baron" Names TSMC and Four Other Quality Stocks to Buy
paras: 晶片股遭遇選舉變局、財報疑慮與終端需求疲弱多重夾擊，半導體類股掀起拋售潮。不過，《巴隆週刊》指出，隨著股價大幅修正，產業估值已降至近三年低點，若人工智慧 (AI) 投資只是放緩，而非全面崩潰，台積電等五家業者，正浮現更具吸引力的布局機會。
《巴隆》週四 (5 日) 報導，iShares 半導體 ETF (SOXX-US) 暴跌12.15%，最近六個交易日有五日下跌。該 ETF 自 10 月初以來累計重挫約 28%，較 6 月 22 日歷史收盤高點回落約 37%，反映市場對晶片產業成長前景的預期快速降溫。
這波跌勢並非單一利空造成，而是個人電腦 (PC)、智慧手機與 AI 資料中心三大市場，同時面臨不同程度的壓力，連供應鏈成本上升也成為企業獲利的阻力。
PC、手機需求疲弱 財報優於預期仍難過關
PC 市場低迷，首先衝擊高度仰賴相關業務的英特爾 (INTC-US)。該公司約半數營收來自 PC 晶片，上週公布第三季 PC 業務萎縮後，股價已累計下跌約 43%。
智慧手機市場同樣疲弱，使高通 (QCOM-US) 與安謀 (Arm)(ARM-US) 承受壓力。兩家公司週三盤後公布的獲利雖優於市場預期，但財報仍有令投資人失望之處，週四股價分別下跌超 9% 與 13%。
此外，高通在財報中警告，零組件成本上漲正影響整條供應鏈，涵蓋晶圓製造、組裝、測試與先進封裝。這意味即使部分市場需求仍強，企業也可能因成本增加或供應受限，難以充分將需求轉化為獲利。
選舉變局衝擊 AI 基建預期
相較於 PC 與手機晶片業者，輝達 (NVDA-US)、博通 (AVGO-US) 與超微 (AMD-US) 等 AI 處理器供應商，以及美光 (MU-US)、SK 海力士與三星電子等記憶體業者，更依賴大型雲端企業對 AI 資料中心的龐大投資。
民主黨在週二期中選舉大勝後，市場開始擔心資料中心擴建速度放緩。投資人關注的範圍不只國會，也包括資料中心重點州的州長、土地與公用事業委員等選舉結果，因為地方政策可能影響建設許可、土地使用與電力供應。
傑富瑞分析師週四在研究報告中，將 2030 年新增資料中心容量預測下修約 8%；瑞銀則估計，原訂於 2028 年上線的容量中，約 30% 如今面臨風險。
這些預測反映的是建設時程與落實程度的不確定性，尚不代表相關容量已確定取消，但已足以促使市場重新評估 AI 晶片需求的成長速度。
股價修正壓低估值 獲利成長預期仍在
儘管利空接連浮現，分析師尚未預期半導體產業獲利將全面衰退。
根據 FactSet 彙整預估，SOXX 投資組合對應的每股盈餘，預料將由 2026 年約 7 美元，增至明年的 10.57 美元，增幅約 51%。
與此同時，估值已大幅回落。SOXX 在 6 月時，未來 12 個月預估本益比一度高達 33 倍，如今降至約 16 倍，為 2023 年以來最低水準。
瑞銀策略師指出，半導體類股在選舉前便已出現估值下修，投資人也大幅削減持股。資料中心建設若減速，對半導體與 AI 基礎建設確實不利，但部分風險可能已反映在股價中。
不過，低本益比仍須建立在獲利預測能夠實現的前提上；若後續需求轉弱，導致分析師下修盈餘，現有估值的吸引力也可能改變。
巴隆看好五家業者 AI 仍是主要成長引擎
《巴隆》表示，該刊今年 5 月曾在晶片股上漲、回檔風險逐漸升高時，推薦輝達、超微、博通、美光與台積電 (TSM-US) 等五家業者。如今股價大幅修正，這五家公司的投資理由仍然成立，核心在於 AI 依舊是半導體產業最重要的成長動力。
即使英特爾 PC 業務表現疲弱，其同季資料中心與 AI 部門營收仍年增 78%，顯示不同終端市場的需求差距相當明顯。
Advisors Capital 投資組合經理費尼 (JoAnne Feeney) 認為，市場對 AI 投資全面崩潰的擔憂可能過度。各州仍需要就業機會與稅收，只要企業妥善處理環境問題，並自行負擔供電成本，地方政府仍有理由歡迎資料中心進駐。
她表示，資料中心建設可能延後，是這波賣壓的原因之一，但她認為最差情況可能也只是延遲。部分個股估值已變得相當有吸引力，其中包括博通與輝達。
報導指出，輝達在週四開盤前的預估本益比僅約 13 倍，較標普 500 指數低約 30%；協助 Alphabet 與 OpenAI 等合作夥伴開發客製化晶片的博通，預估本益比則不到 16 倍。
低估值能否成為買點 仍取決於訂單兌現
《巴隆》也提醒，估值仍可能進一步下滑，AI 產業另有大型客戶履約能力的風險。
其中，Anthropic 已作出近 9,000 億美元的供應承諾。若未能落實，相關供應商可能失去部分原先預期的需求，衝擊訂單與獲利前景。
不過，該刊認為，過去一週的股價跌勢，主要仍與選舉結果及資料中心建設疑慮有關，與 Anthropic 的關聯有限。若 AI 投資未走向全面崩潰，近期修正便可能讓幾個月前仍顯昂貴的優質晶片股，出現更合理的進場價格。
paras_en: Chip stocks are hit by a triple whammy of election upheaval, earnings doubts and weak end‑user demand, sparking a sell‑off in semiconductor equities. However, Baron Weekly notes that with prices sharply corrected, industry valuations have fallen to near three‑year lows; if AI investment merely slows rather than collapses, TSMC and four other firms present increasingly attractive positioning opportunities.

Baron reported on Thursday (the 5th) that the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX‑US) tumbled 12.15%, falling on five of the last six trading days. The ETF has lost about 28% since early October and is down roughly 37% from its June 22 historical closing high, reflecting a rapid cooling of market expectations for chip‑industry growth.

The decline is not driven by a single negative factor; the PC, smartphone and AI data‑center markets are all under varying degrees of pressure, and rising supply‑chain costs are also hampering corporate profits.
PC and smartphone demand weak; earnings beat expectations but still fall short

The slump in the PC market first hit Intel (INTC‑US), which derives about half of its revenue from PC chips. After reporting a contraction in its third‑quarter PC business last week, the stock has fallen roughly 43% in total.

Weak smartphone demand is also weighing on Qualcomm (QCOM‑US) and Arm (ARM‑US). Both companies posted earnings on Wednesday after market close that beat forecasts, yet the reports contained disappointing elements, and their shares fell more than 9% and 13% respectively on Thursday.

In addition, Qualcomm warned in its earnings release that rising component costs are affecting the entire supply chain, from wafer fabrication to assembly, testing and advanced packaging. This means that even if some market demand remains strong, companies may struggle to translate it into profit due to higher costs or constrained supply.
Election upheaval dents AI‑infrastructure expectations

Compared with PC and smartphone chipmakers, AI‑processor suppliers such as Nvidia (NVDA‑US), Broadcom (AVGO‑US) and AMD (AMD‑US), as well as memory makers like Micron (MU‑US), SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, rely more heavily on massive AI data‑center investments from large cloud providers.

After the Democrats’ sweeping victory in Tuesday’s midterm elections, the market began to worry that data‑center expansion could slow. Investors are watching not only Congress but also the outcomes of gubernatorial, land‑use and utility commission races in key data‑center states, since local policies can affect construction permits, land use and power supply.

Jefferies analysts cut their 2030 new data‑center capacity forecast by about 8% in a Thursday research note; UBS estimates that roughly 30% of the capacity originally slated for launch by 2028 now faces risk.

These forecasts reflect uncertainty around construction timelines and implementation, not a definitive cancellation of capacity, but they are enough to prompt the market to reassess the growth rate of AI‑chip demand.
Price corrections depress valuations but earnings‑growth expectations remain
Despite the string of negatives, analysts do not expect semiconductor industry earnings to enter a full‑scale decline.
FactSet’s consensus estimate shows that the SOXX portfolio’s earnings per share are projected to rise from about $7 in 2026 to $10.57 next year, an increase of roughly 51%.
At the same time, valuations have fallen sharply. In June, SOXX’s forward 12‑month price‑to‑earnings ratio peaked at 33×, but it now sits near 16×, the lowest level since 2023.

UBS strategists note that semiconductor stocks had already seen valuation cuts before the election, and investors have significantly trimmed holdings. Slower data‑center builds are indeed a headwind for chips and AI infrastructure, but much of the risk appears to be priced into the stocks.
However, a low P/E ratio only makes sense if earnings forecasts can be met; if demand weakens further and analysts downgrade earnings, the current valuation appeal could evaporate.
Baron bullish on five firms; AI remains the main growth engine

Baron said that in May, when chip stocks were rising but pull‑back risk was increasing, it recommended Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC (TSM‑US). With prices now sharply corrected, the investment thesis for these five remains intact, centered on AI still being the semiconductor sector’s key growth driver.
Even though Intel’s PC business is struggling, its data‑center and AI segment revenue grew 78% year‑over‑year in the same quarter, highlighting a stark contrast in demand across end markets.

Advisors Capital portfolio manager JoAnne Feeney believes concerns that AI investment will collapse entirely may be overstated. States still need jobs and tax revenue; as long as companies address environmental issues and cover their own power costs, local governments have reason to welcome data‑centers.

She says that delayed data‑center construction is one factor behind the current selling pressure, but she views the worst‑case scenario as merely a postponement. Some stocks have become quite attractive, including Broadcom and Nvidia.

The report notes that Nvidia’s estimated forward P/E before Thursday’s open was about 13×, roughly 30% below the S&P 500 average; Broadcom, which helps partners such as Alphabet and OpenAI develop custom chips, is estimated at under 16×.
Will low valuations become buying points? It still depends on order fulfillment
Baron also cautions that valuations could slip further, and the AI sector faces risk from the execution capability of large customers.
Among them, Anthropic has pledged roughly $900 billion in supply commitments. If it fails to deliver, suppliers could lose part of the demand they had expected, hurting orders and profit outlooks.

Nevertheless, the magazine believes the recent week’s price decline was mainly tied to election outcomes and data‑center construction concerns, with limited connection to Anthropic. If AI investment does not collapse entirely, the recent correction could make previously pricey quality chip stocks a more reasonably priced entry point.

items.title: 牛彈琴：美期中大選後次日華爾街暴跌　10大嚴重後果顯現
items.title_en: Bull Playing the Piano: Wall Street Plummets the Day After the US Midterms, Ten Severe Consequences Emerge
paras: 美股大跌之際，具中國官方背景微信公眾號「牛彈琴」今(6) 日刊文表示，美國本屆期中選舉至少帶來十個深遠的嚴重後果。
首先是市場信心的斷崖式 。選舉次日美股還因押注AI支出放緩而大漲，但隨即在當地時間周四(5日)迎來「清醒」時刻，那斯達重挫5.52%，科技七巨頭市值單日蒸發逾1兆美元。投資者恐懼的不再是單一政黨，而是兩黨惡鬥帶來的政策真空與極度不確定性。
其次，美國政壇進入極度撕裂期。總統川普提前戴上「否決權」紅帽，預示其將成為「跛鴨」總統。隨著民主黨掌控國會，傳票權成為制衡白宮的利器，川普家族生意、伊朗戰爭決策及人事清洗都將面臨嚴厲審查，彈劾陰影重新籠罩華盛頓。
在人事與黨內動向方面，失敗的代價正在清算。美國防長赫格塞斯因伊朗戰爭失利面臨下台壓力；副總統范斯則發表「非同尋常」長文，將敗因歸咎於戰爭並與川普切割，共和黨內部分裂出「挺川」與「挺范」兩大派系，2028年總統大選的算盤已提前打響。
財政與經濟危機同步升級。隨著12月11日臨時撥款截止日與債務上限「X日」臨近，民主黨極可能利用預算談判卡住川普喉嚨，要求恢復醫保補貼或限制關稅，政府關門恐成常態。此外，民主黨在州一級實現「三權全控」，將在移民、墮胎及氣候議題上與聯邦政府形成「平行對抗」，紅藍兩州正活成兩個美國。
外交與國際信用亦受重創。川普突然宣布終止對以色列每年40億美元的援助，顯示美以「特殊關係」出現裂痕。更深層的隱憂在於美元信用的鬆動，一個連預算都吵不出結果的政府，正加劇全球去美元化的意願。
對世界而言，這場選舉釋放一個信號，也就是與美國簽署的協議，保質期可能僅有兩年。歐洲正加速「戰略自主」，俄羅斯與新興市場則在重新評估博弈籌碼。
當山姆大叔忙於內耗，世界格局進入了高度動盪的「後美國共識」時代。大國博弈的下半場，比的不再是拳頭，而是誰的家底更穩、腳步更定。好戲，真的還在後頭。
paras_en: Amid the US stock market crash, the WeChat public account "Bull Playing the Piano," which has ties to Chinese officials, posted today (the 6th) that the current US midterm election will bring at least ten far‑reaching severe consequences.

First, market confidence has collapsed like a cliff. The day after the election US stocks surged on bets that AI spending would slow, but on Thursday (the 5th) a "wake‑up" moment arrived, with Nvidia tumbling 5.52% and the seven big tech firms wiping out more than $1 trillion in market value in a single day. Investors now fear not a single party but the policy vacuum and extreme uncertainty created by bipartisan infighting.

Second, US politics has entered a period of extreme division. President Trump has pre‑emptively donned a "veto" red hat, signalling he will become a "lame‑duck" president. With Democrats controlling Congress, the power of subpoenas becomes a tool to check the White House, and Trump‑related businesses, Iran war decisions and personnel purges will face harsh scrutiny, reviving impeachment shadows over Washington.

In personnel and intra‑party dynamics, the cost of failure is being settled. Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin (referred to as "Hugheses" in the original) faces pressure to resign over setbacks in the Iran war; Vice President Harris (mis‑named "Fans") issued an "unusual" long‑form statement blaming the war for the loss and distancing herself from Trump, splitting the GOP into "pro‑Trump" and "pro‑Harris" camps and kicking off the calculus for the 2028 presidential race early.

Fiscal and economic crises are escalating together. With the temporary funding deadline on Dec 11 and the debt‑limit "X‑day" approaching, Democrats are likely to use budget negotiations to choke Trump, demanding the restoration of Medicare subsidies or tariff limits, making government shutdowns a new normal. Moreover, Democrats achieving "full‑control" of state‑level three‑branch power will create parallel confrontations with the federal government on immigration, abortion and climate, turning red and blue states into two separate Americas.

Diplomacy and international credit are also severely hit. Trump’s sudden announcement to end the annual $4 billion aid to Israel shows cracks in the US‑Israel "special relationship." A deeper worry is the loosening of dollar credibility; a government that cannot even agree on a budget fuels global de‑dollarisation momentum.

For the world, the election sends a signal that agreements signed with the US may only have a two‑year shelf life. Europe is accelerating its "strategic autonomy," while Russia and emerging markets are re‑evaluating their bargaining chips.

While Uncle Sam is busy with internal strife, the global order has entered a highly volatile "post‑American consensus" era. The second half of great‑power competition is no longer about who throws the hardest punch, but whose balance sheets are sturdier and steps more decisive. The real drama is still to come.

items.title: 川普稱俄烏將達成重大協議 範圍可能涵蓋整個歐洲
items.title_en: Trump Says Russia‑Ukraine Deal Will Be Major, Possibly Covering All of Europe
paras: 美國總統川普5日在白宮向媒體表示，將就俄烏問題達成「重大協議」，並稱距離解決俄烏問題已「非常接近」。他指出，協議涉及範圍不僅限於烏克蘭，甚至可能涵蓋整個歐洲。
川普表示，他已在白宮會見俄羅斯總統特別代表德米特里耶夫，但未會見烏克蘭代表，並拒絕透露會談具體內容。
同日，美國第一夫人梅蘭妮亞也在白宮就俄烏順利實施奧列什基停火，會見俄烏官員。出席者包括德米特里耶夫、烏克蘭執政黨人民公僕黨國會黨團主席阿拉哈米亞，以及烏克蘭國會人權事務專員盧比涅茨。
在歐洲安全議題方面，川普女婿庫許納5日在社群媒體發文表示，美國當天與烏克蘭、北約及歐洲夥伴在布魯塞爾進行富有成效且實質性的討論，議題涵蓋對烏克蘭的安全保障，以及更廣泛的歐洲安全架構。
此外，美國總統特使威特科夫2日已在社群媒體宣布，美方將於10日至11日在阿拉伯聯合大公國首都阿布達比，斡旋烏克蘭與俄羅斯之間的工作層級談判，以推動結束俄烏衝突。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump told the press at the White House on the 5th that a "major agreement" on the Russia‑Ukraine issue will be reached, saying the resolution of the conflict is "very close." He noted that the agreement’s scope would not be limited to Ukraine and could even encompass the entire continent of Europe.
Trump said he had met at the White House with Russia’s special representative Dmitriyev, but had not met with any Ukrainian representatives, and he declined to disclose the specifics of their talks.

On the same day, First Lady Melania Trump also met at the White House with Russian and Ukrainian officials to discuss the smooth implementation of the Oleshky cease‑fire. Attendees included Dmitriyev, Ukrainian ruling party People's Servants Party parliamentary caucus chair Alakhamiya, and Ukrainian parliamentary human‑rights commissioner Rubynets.

Regarding European security, Trump’s son‑in‑law Kushner posted on social media on the 5th that the United States that day held productive, substantive discussions in Brussels with Ukraine, NATO and European partners, covering security guarantees for Ukraine and a broader European security architecture.

In addition, U.S. Special Envoy Whitmore announced on social media on the 2nd that the United States will mediate work‑level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on October 10‑11, aiming to push toward an end to the Russia‑Ukraine conflict.

items.title_en: 'Blue Tide' Sparks AI Infrastructure Concerns! Nasdaq Plunges, Erasing $2.5 Trillion in Market Value in One Day – What’s Next?
paras: 隨著民主黨在美國中期選舉中全面掌控國會，市場對AI基礎建設放緩的擔憂發酵，美股科技股週四(5日)遭遇歷史性暴跌。那斯達克綜合指數單日重挫5.52%，創2025年4月「解放日」關稅政策以來最大單日跌幅，較上月歷史高點回落11%，正式進入回調區域。
晶片股成為重災區。iShares半導體ETF暴跌12%，創2020年3月以來最差單日表現；費城半導體指數狂瀉12.25%。根據估算，那指成分股市值當日蒸發約2.5兆美元，科技七巨頭合計損失約1.04兆美元。
引發本輪拋售的導火索是民主黨在多個資料中心「重鎮」取得重大勝利，例如德州當選州長主張立即暫停AI資料中心建設。投資者擔憂州層面的嚴格限制將拖累AI基建擴張，重創相關企業估值。
不過，「以史為鑒」的技術性分析顯示，市場短期承壓但中長期仍有支撐。過去十年10次那斯達克回調統計顯示，短期雖可能面臨進一步拋售，但在觸底後的三個月內平均反彈9.41%，六個月內平均漲幅達17.03%。
CappThesis創辦人Frank Cappelleri指出，自1974年以來的13個期中選舉周期中，有12次選舉後12個月內那指都實現上漲。儘管短期波動難免，但歷史規律暗示，科技股在消化政策利空後，有望重啟修復行情。
paras_en: As Democrats take full control of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, worries about a slowdown in AI infrastructure have fermented, leading U.S. tech stocks to suffer a historic crash on Thursday (the 5th). The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% in a single day, the biggest one‑day drop since the “Liberation Day” tariff policy in April 2025, and slid 11% from last month’s all‑time high, officially entering correction territory.

Chip stocks bore the brunt. The iShares Semiconductor ETF tumbled 12%, marking its worst single‑day performance since March 2020; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25%. Estimates show that Nasdaq component market capitalisation evaporated about $2.5 trillion that day, with the seven big tech giants collectively losing roughly $1.04 trillion.

The catalyst for this round of selling was the Democrats’ major victories in several data‑center strongholds, such as Texas, where the newly elected governor pledged to immediately halt AI data‑center construction. Investors fear that strict state‑level restrictions will drag down AI infrastructure expansion and severely dent valuations of related companies.

However, a “learn‑from‑history” technical analysis indicates that while the market is under short‑term pressure, medium‑ to long‑term support remains. Statistics from the past ten Nasdaq pullbacks over the last decade show that, although further short‑term selling is possible, the index has on average rebounded 9.41% within three months after bottoming and gained 17.03% on average within six months.

Frank Cappelleri, founder of CappThesis, notes that in 12 of the 13 midterm election cycles since 1974, the Nasdaq has risen within twelve months after the election. While short‑term volatility is inevitable, this historical pattern suggests that after digesting policy‑related headwinds, tech stocks are likely to resume a recovery rally.

U.S. September trade deficit narrowed 0.7% from the prior month to $105.0 billion. The ADP national employment report showed that private-sector jobs in the United States increased by 86,000 in October, with September's increase revised down to 86,000. Rating agency Scope said the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory supports the U.S. AA‑minus rating with a stable outlook. According to a S&P Global survey, Japan’s October services PMI final reading rose slightly from September’s 51.3 to 51.7, indicating modest expansion in Japanese services activity. In addition, the Bank of Japan’s September meeting minutes revealed that BOJ policymakers believe further rate hikes are necessary, with one official hinting that the pace of tightening could accelerate. Market concerns about the Democrats regaining control of Congress and a shift in political winds could affect the AI sector outlook, causing U.S. equities to plunge and pushing the dollar‑yen down to a low of 157.52.

U.S. data released for the week ending October 31 showed initial unemployment claims fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000, the lowest level since 1957. U.S. companies announced 43,994 layoffs in October, the lowest since early 2023. Third‑quarter non‑farm productivity rose 3.6% year‑over‑year, beating expectations. Cleveland Fed President Mester said that because price pressures remain unacceptably high, the Federal Reserve still needs additional action to bring inflation back to its 2% target. Fed Governor Bostic noted that inflation has not eased, making a gradual rate‑hike path reasonable, which lifted the dollar‑yen to a high of 158.49. The dollar‑yen resistance today is estimated at 157.80‑158.00, with support at 157.00‑157.20.
EUR/USD

Australia’s Bureau of Statistics reported a September goods trade surplus of A$2.83 billion (US$1.98 billion), up from August’s A$184 million. As concerns over a potential attack on Iran eased, oil prices fell, market sentiment improved, risk assets rallied, and the Australian and New Zealand dollars continued to rise, supporting a higher euro‑dollar exchange rate.

The euro‑area September producer price index rose 2.5% month‑over‑month and 11.1% year‑over‑year, beating forecasts. The German Federation of Industries raised its 2026 German growth forecast from 0.3% to 1%, pushing the euro‑dollar up to a high of 1.1268. However, Germany’s federal statistics office said September industrial orders, seasonally and calendar‑adjusted, grew 4.4% month‑over‑month, below the expected 4.8%, pulling the euro‑dollar down to a low of 1.1202. The euro‑dollar resistance today is estimated at 1.1255‑1.1275, with support at 1.1190‑1.1210.

The BOE signaled that policy could tighten further. Governor Andrew Bailey said that if the Iran conflict continues to push energy prices higher and raise inflation risks, another rate hike may be needed, lifting the pound‑dollar to a high of 1.3506. Subsequently, S&P Global’s UK construction PMI fell from 46.1 in September to 43.6 in October, below expectations and indicating the fastest contraction in the sector since June, which pulled the pound‑dollar down to a low of 1.3444. items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元遊走平盤 投資人憂AI發展煞車影響經濟成長
items.title_en: <New York Forex> Dollar Flat as Investors Worry AI Development Slowdown Could Hit Growth
paras: 美元對主要貨幣周四(5日)遊走平盤，油價在前一交易日大幅下跌後反彈，投資人則正評估人工智慧(AI)相關支出一旦放緩拖累經濟成長的風險。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣走勢的ICE美元指數(DXY)小幅上漲0.02%，報101.49，DXY曾在前一交易日創下三周來最大單日跌幅。
歐元兌美元升值0.02%，報1.1229美元。
美股周四也大幅走低，標普500科技類股指數(SPLRCT)重挫逾6%，拖累整體市場。市場對AI相關企業龐大支出的疑慮再度浮現，加上監管措施可能進一步增加，恐拖慢這項新興技術所需基礎設施的建置速度。
民主黨承諾將利用期中選舉的壓倒性勝利制衡總統川普，使華府未來兩年可能陷入政治僵局。

強勁就業數據支撐Fed升息預期

投資人也在等待周五公布的非農就業報告。美國勞工部周四公布的數據顯示，上周初領失業救濟金人數減少6,000人，經季節性調整後降至18.9萬人，與今年7月創下的57年低點持平，也低於經濟學家預估的19.6萬人。
其他數據方面，美國第3季勞工生產力增幅優於預期，有助於壓低勞動成本，也支持勞動市場並非通膨來源的看法。
Convera首席外匯與總體策略師Kevin Ford說：「部分原因是油價反彈……基本上，本周公布的數據強勁到足以支持美國就業市場仍保持穩定的看法，這也有助於支撐市場對Fed年底及明年初連續升息的預期。」
Ford表示，市場目前預期AI基礎建設投資放緩，因此正在調整對長期經濟成長前景的看法。但短期而言，美國經濟基本面仍相當穩健，足以讓Fed繼續升息，市場也正趕在非農就業報告公布前，提前布局這項預期。
儘管美國政治局勢出現變化，且原油價格下跌，市場對Fed利率展望的看法仍大致持平。根據芝商所(CME)FedWatch工具，市場目前預估Fed 12月會議至少升息1碼(25個基點)的機率為66.1%，低於一周前的79.9%。
克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁哈瑪克(Beth Hammack)表示，要讓通膨降至2%的目標，Fed仍有更多工作要做，目前物價壓力仍高得令人無法接受。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁巴金(Tom Barkin)則表示，循序漸進升息「是合理的」。
歐洲央行(ECB)管理委員會成員Isabel Schnabel表示，公共債務增加及非銀行金融業快速擴張，可能限制ECB制定適當貨幣政策的能力。
另一方面，揮舞旗幟的抗議民眾周四走上法國各大城市街頭，公部門員工也發起罷工，凸顯市場對法國財政走向的疑慮仍未消退。

英國央行升息 英鎊走低

英鎊貶值0.09%至1.3457美元。英鎊周四稍早曾升至逾七周高點，英國央行宣布三年多來首度升息，並警告若美伊衝突持續，至少還可能再升息一次。
日本銀行(BOJ，央行)公布9月會議紀錄後，日元升值0.46%至1美元兌157.63日元。日銀決策官員該月將基準利率調升至31年來高點1.25%，進一步強化市場對日本繼續升息的押注。
會議紀錄顯示，部分決策官員釋出可能加快升息步調的訊號。日銀決策委員會也討論中性利率，以及市場對終端利率的預期，顯示央行日益關注，在不致過度壓抑經濟的情況下，利率究竟還能調升多少。
高盛分析師周四指出，日元是對沖AI風險的最佳貨幣。當那斯達克指數表現落後標普500指數時，美元兌日元通常會走貶，若那斯達克落後幅度超過1%，美元跌幅還會更大。
另外，巴克萊分析師表示，長期而言，日元走勢愈來愈不受油價影響，轉而與全球市場風險情緒同步；「但在油價較高的時期，日元走勢明顯偏弱，與這項長期趨勢出現顯著背離。」

paras_en: The dollar was flat against major currencies on Thursday (the 5th), oil prices rebounded after a sharp drop the previous session, and investors are assessing the risk that a slowdown in AI‑related spending could drag on economic growth.

In the New York close, the ICE Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, edged up 0.02% to 101.49, after posting the biggest single‑day decline in three weeks on the prior trading day.
The euro rose 0.02% against the dollar to $1.1229.

U.S. equities also fell sharply on Thursday, with the S&P 500 technology index (SPLRCT) plunging more than 6%, pulling down the broader market. Concerns about massive AI‑related corporate spending resurfaced, and potential regulatory measures could further slow the build‑out of infrastructure needed for the emerging technology.
Democrats pledged to use their overwhelming mid‑term election victory to check President Trump, leaving Washington potentially mired in a political stalemate for the next two years.

Strong employment data underpin Fed rate‑hike expectations. Investors are also awaiting Friday’s non‑farm payroll report. Labor Department figures released Thursday showed initial unemployment claims fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000, matching the 57‑year low set in July and below economists’ forecast of 196,000.
Other data showed U.S. third‑quarter labor productivity exceeded expectations, helping to keep labor costs down and supporting the view that the labor market is not the source of inflation.

Convera chief foreign‑exchange and macro strategist Kevin Ford said, “Part of it is the oil price rebound… Basically, the data released this week are strong enough to support the view that the U.S. job market remains stable, which also helps underpin market expectations of consecutive Fed hikes through year‑end and early next year.”

Ford added that the market currently expects AI infrastructure investment to slow, prompting a revision of long‑term growth outlooks. In the short term, however, the U.S. economy’s fundamentals remain solid enough for the Fed to keep raising rates, and markets are positioning ahead of the payroll release.

Despite shifts in U.S. politics and lower crude prices, views on the Fed’s rate path remain broadly unchanged. CME FedWatch data show the probability of at least a 25‑basis‑point hike at the December meeting is 66.1%, down from 79.9% a week earlier.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said more work is needed to bring inflation down to the 2% target and that price pressures remain unacceptably high. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin described a gradual rate‑hike approach as “reasonable.”
ECB Governing Council member Isabel Schnabel warned that rising public debt and rapid expansion of the non‑bank financial sector could limit the ECB’s ability to set appropriate monetary policy.

Meanwhile, protestors waving flags took to the streets of major French cities on Thursday, and public‑sector workers staged strikes, underscoring lingering market concerns over France’s fiscal direction.

British pound down 0.09% to $1.3457. The pound had earlier risen to a seven‑week high on Thursday after the Bank of England announced its first rate hike in over three years and warned that if the U.S.–Iran conflict persists, another increase is possible.

After the Bank of Japan released September meeting minutes, the yen rose 0.46% to ¥157.63 per $1. The BOJ’s policy‑making officials had lifted the benchmark rate to a 31‑year high of 1.25% that month, reinforcing market bets on further Japanese rate hikes.

The minutes showed some officials signalling a possible acceleration of the tightening pace. The BOJ board also discussed the neutral rate and market expectations for the terminal rate, indicating growing concern about how much higher rates can go without overly suppressing the economy.

Goldman Sachs analysts noted on Thursday that the yen is the best currency hedge against AI risk. When the Nasdaq underperforms the S&P 500, the dollar typically weakens against the yen, and if the Nasdaq lag exceeds 1%, the dollar’s decline is even larger.

Barclays analysts added that, over the long term, the yen is becoming less tied to oil prices and more aligned with global risk sentiment; however, during periods of higher oil prices the yen’s move is noticeably weaker, diverging sharply from that long‑term trend.

items.title_en: Foreign Capital Withdrawal Mass Exodus: October Outflows About NT$9 Trillion Set New Record; Central Bank: Intervened to Prevent Depreciation
paras: 中央銀行今(5)日公布10月底我國外匯存底金額為5964.37億美元，月減 43.08億美元，跌破6000億美元關卡，創3個月來低點，央行指出，10月外資淨匯出約280億美元(含盈餘匯出)創單月新高，折合新台幣約9000億元，因此為維持外匯市場秩序，有進場調節阻貶，使新台幣單月僅貶值2.29%。
央行統計，外資持有國內股票及債券按當日市價計算，連同其新台幣存款餘額共折計1兆7426億美元，約當外匯存底292%則創5月以來低。
央行強調，不會刻意改變匯市方向，但不樂見看到匯率波動太大，會有一些調節以維持動態穩定。
此外，央行統計主要國家的外匯存底，中國降至3兆4003億美元，日本也降至9769億美元，印度為5932億美元，南韓為4187億美元。
對於新台幣近期貶值甚至在今日觸及33元整數大關，央行表示，廠商可能有所期待，但「不認為它會一直持續下去」，也表態「希望大家主要是實質拋補，不要有太大一個期待」，並重申「希望年底前廠商的結匯需求能夠多出來一點」的立場。
paras_en: The central bank announced today (the 5th) that Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves stood at $5,964.37 billion at the end of October, a monthly decline of $4.308 billion, slipping below the $6 trillion threshold and hitting a three‑month low. The bank noted that net foreign capital outflows in October amounted to about $28 billion (including profit repatriation), a record high for a single month, equivalent to roughly NT$9 trillion. To maintain order in the FX market, the bank stepped in to curb further depreciation, limiting the New Taiwan dollar’s monthly loss to just 2.29%.

According to the central bank’s calculations, foreign investors’ holdings of domestic stocks and bonds, valued at market prices and combined with their New Taiwan dollar deposits, totalled about $1.7426 trillion, which is roughly 292% of the foreign exchange reserves—a low not seen since May.

The central bank emphasized that it will not deliberately steer the exchange‑rate direction, but it is uneasy about excessive volatility and will make adjustments as needed to preserve dynamic stability.

In addition, the bank’s statistics on major countries’ foreign exchange reserves show China’s reserves falling to $3.4003 trillion, Japan’s to $976.9 billion, India’s at $593.2 billion, and South Korea’s at $418.7 billion.

Regarding the recent depreciation of the New Taiwan dollar, which even touched the round figure of 33 NT$ today, the central bank said that while market participants might have expectations, "we do not believe it will continue indefinitely." It urged firms to focus on real hedging rather than harboring large expectations and reiterated its hope that firms’ settlement‑demand for foreign exchange will increase before year‑end.

items.title: 挪威央行維持利率4.5%不變 總裁仍警告通膨過高 保留升息選項
items.title_en: Norway Central Bank Keeps Rate at 4.5% as Governor Warns Inflation Still Too High, Leaves Rate‑Hike Option Open
paras: 挪威央行周四(5日)將基準存款利率維持在4.5%的高點不變，符合媒體調查中分析師的預測，然而，央行政策制定者重申，若有需要抑止通膨，仍保留再次升息的選項。
針對利率政策與物價前景，挪威央行總裁Ida Wolden Bache在官方聲明中表示通膨過高。他進一步強調：「政策利率可能需要在一段時間內保持高位，若需要將通膨率降至目標，我們已準備好調升政策利率。」
雖然這個富含能源的國家在夏季的通膨放緩超乎預期，但官員們仍面臨全面平抑物價成長的挑戰。自2022年以來，挪威通膨持續顯著高於目標，部分原因係央行優先考慮維持低失業率，官方目前預估要到2029年才能實現2%的通膨目標。
在國內經濟方面，由於本土經濟持續擴張，薪資壓力僅漸進放緩，少數派工黨內閣在與盟友協商後的明年預算可能更具擴張性，為物價添增上行壓力。然而，挪威克朗今年做為G10國家中表現最強勁者，貨幣走高正降低進口通膨的風險。
經濟學家指出，克朗走強可能讓挪威利率制定者在本輪周期免於額外升息，儘管投資人仍反映明年3月會議升息機率約有50%。
與此同時，全球其他央行正積極進行緊縮。鄰國瑞典央行周三實施了自2023年以來的首次升息，市場廣泛預期英國央行將在周四稍晚調升利率。
paras_en: On Thursday (the 5th), Norway’s central bank kept its policy deposit rate unchanged at the high level of 4.5%, matching analysts’ expectations in media surveys. However, policymakers reiterated that they still retain the option to raise rates again if needed to curb inflation.

Regarding rate policy and price outlook, Norges Bank Governor Ida Wolden Bache said in an official statement that inflation remains too high. She added, “The policy rate may need to stay elevated for a period of time; if we need to bring inflation down to target, we are ready to raise the policy rate further.”

Although this energy‑rich country saw summer inflation ease more than expected, officials still face the challenge of broadly tempering price growth. Since 2022, Norwegian inflation has stayed well above target, partly because the central bank has prioritized keeping unemployment low. The authorities now estimate that the 2% inflation goal will not be reached until 2029.

Domestically, the economy continues to expand and wage pressures are only gradually easing. A minority‑led Labour government, after negotiations with its coalition partners, may present a more expansionary budget for next year, adding upward pressure on prices. Meanwhile, the Norwegian krone has been the strongest performer among G10 currencies this year, and its appreciation is reducing the risk of imported inflation.

Economists note that a stronger krone could spare Norway’s rate‑setters from needing an additional hike in this cycle, although investors still price roughly a 50% chance of a rate increase at the March meeting next year.

At the same time, other central banks around the world are actively tightening. Neighboring Sweden’s central bank implemented its first rate hike since 2023 on Wednesday, and markets widely expect the Bank of England to raise rates later on Thursday.

items.title: 新台幣要逢低反轉了？外匯局長對近期匯市給這些說法
items.title_en: Is the New Taiwan Dollar Set to Reverse on Lows? The Central Bank's Forex Chief Comments on Recent Market Moves
paras: 新台幣今(5)日爆出成交天量，台北外匯經紀公司成交值衝上36.56億美元，最低也一度貶至32.985元，創去年4月以來新低，中央銀行外匯局長蔡烱民表示，匯價本是動態調整，「沒有什麼數字才是合不合理」，但也強調，「有感覺外資賣超已有收斂情形」，且「年底前國內廠商會出來進行結售，不會一直持續下去」；外界解讀，央行在帶頭信心喊話。
蔡烱民表示，近期外資賣超幅度和11月跌點，數據拿來對照10月跌點，其實近日外資賣超有在收斂情形，不過，「只是一個趨勢，還不是很一定，央行會密切觀察變動情形」。
蔡烱民強調，新台幣貶值最主要還是反映外資匯出，「波動大都是不好的」，央行會關注匯市供需是否平衡，並再次指出，台灣基本面和國際收支都非常好，今年以來至今新台幣貶值因素約4%左右，跟過去相比並非很特別的幅度，只是比較集中在最近，才讓市場有感。
蔡烱民進一步提及，時序近年底，廠商須有所結算，「年底前會出來結售，就不會一直持續下去，觀察到這幾天廠商賣匯金額有增加」。
同時，蔡烱民認為，「外資一旦回頭，力道也會非常高」。
paras_en: The New Taiwan dollar saw a massive trading volume today (the 5th), with a Taipei foreign‑exchange brokerage reporting a transaction value of US$3.656 billion and the rate briefly slipping to NT$32.985, the lowest since April last year. Central Bank Foreign Exchange Director Cai Jung‑min said the exchange rate is naturally dynamic – “there’s no single number that is unreasonable” – but noted that “it feels like foreign‑capital net selling is already easing” and that “domestic firms will settle and unwind positions before year‑end, so the decline won’t continue indefinitely,” a statement interpreted as the central bank trying to boost confidence.

Cai explained that the recent net‑selling by foreign investors and the November dip, when compared with the October dip, show that foreign‑capital outflows have been narrowing lately. However, he cautioned that this is only a trend and not yet certain, adding that the central bank will closely monitor any changes.

He emphasized that the main driver of the NT$ depreciation is foreign‑capital outflows and that “large volatility is undesirable.” The central bank will watch whether supply and demand in the FX market remain balanced, and reiterated that Taiwan’s fundamentals and external balances are very strong. So far this year, the NT$ has weakened by about 4%, which is not a particularly large move historically; the recent concentration of that decline is what the market is feeling.

Cai added that, as we approach year‑end, companies will need to settle their positions. “They will come out to settle and unwind before the end of the year, so the downward pressure won’t persist, and we have observed an increase in the amount of foreign‑exchange sold by firms in the past few days,” he said.
He also said that “once foreign investors turn back, their buying power will be very strong.”

items.title: 1958年來最慘！《紐約客》評共和黨崩盤：美國的復仇、對川普的否決
items.title_en: The Worst Since 1958! The New Yorker Says the GOP Crumbled: America’s Revenge and a Veto on Trump
paras: 2026年美國期中選舉以一場對現任總統所在政黨的「毀滅性打擊」落幕。民主黨橫掃國會，多個傳統紅州翻藍。這場被視為對川普及其政策「全民公投」的選舉，引發白宮劇烈震盪。總統川普拒絕承擔責任，副總統范斯則罕見承認選民倒戈的殘酷現實。
《紐約客》雜誌專欄作家Susan B. Glasser週三(4日)撰文指出，選舉之夜未過晚上11點，川普才首次發聲。過去幾週，他堅稱選舉是對其個人的公投，但面對慘敗，他第一時間在社群媒體推卸責任：「我不在選票上，如果我在，我們肯定會大獲全勝！」
隨後，他指責德州州長阿博特變成「名義上的共和黨人」，還抱怨《福斯新聞》「不斷播放民主黨反對節目」。
週三早上，川普接受《福斯新聞》採訪時仍堅稱「我不應感到內疚」，白宮隨後還發布川普坐在堅毅桌後的照片，並配上一行文字：「重要提示：川普仍是你們的總統」，試圖強調其執政合法性。
與川普否認形成對比的是，范斯週三早上承認：「主要問題是，許多在2024年投票給川普跟范斯的人，今年卻投給民主黨，他甚至將敗因歸咎於伊朗戰爭，稱「我們失敗的原因就是這場戰爭」。
文中指出，此次選舉是自1974年尼克森下台前，美國總統遭遇到的最徹底否決的一場大選。共和黨在眾議院恐失至少35席，參議院失去多達8席，規模僅見於1958年。選民不滿情緒強烈且多元，普通共和黨選民表達了對川普政策及政黨的「道德厭惡」。
除伊朗戰爭外，柴油價格逼近每加侖7美元、關稅與貿易戰、背叛烏克蘭、政府官員自我斂財、資料中心擴張以及馬斯克等富豪干預選舉，均成為選民投票反對的理由。
川普最後一個月的競選活動，21天內舉行21場集會，大談奇怪話題，並貶低選民對住房負擔能力的擔憂，更被指加劇了選民疏離。
儘管川普試圖將失敗歸咎於一切外部因素，但他私下告訴《紐約時報》，他「絕對願意」接受選舉結果。這場選舉不僅重塑了華府權力格局，更成為美國選民對川普時代的一次清晰清算。
paras_en: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections ended with a "devastating blow" to the incumbent president’s party. Democrats swept Congress, flipping several traditional red states blue. The election, seen as a nationwide referendum on Trump and his policies, sent shockwaves through the White House. President Trump refused to take responsibility, while Vice President Pence unusually acknowledged the harsh reality of voters defecting.

New Yorker columnist Susan B. Glasser wrote on Wednesday (the 4th) that Trump did not speak until after 11 p.m. on election night. In the weeks leading up to the vote he had insisted the election was a personal referendum, but after the crushing loss he immediately shifted blame on social media: "I’m not on the ballot; if I were, we would have won hands down!"
He then blamed Texas Governor Abbott for becoming a "nominal Republican" and complained that Fox News was "continuously airing anti‑Democratic programming."

On Wednesday morning, Trump told Fox News that he "should not feel guilty," and the White House later released a photo of him seated behind a sturdy desk with the caption: "Important note: Trump is still your president," attempting to underscore his legitimacy.

In contrast, Pence on Wednesday morning admitted: "The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump and me in 2024 voted for the Democrats this year," and even blamed the loss on the Iran war, saying, "The reason we lost is this war."

The article notes this election is the most thorough repudiation of a U.S. president since Nixon’s resignation in 1974. Republicans risk losing at least 35 seats in the House and up to eight in the Senate, a scale not seen since 1958. Voter anger is strong and diverse, with ordinary GOP voters expressing "moral disgust" toward Trump’s policies and the party.

Beyond the Iran war, factors such as diesel prices nearing $7 per gallon, tariffs and trade wars, perceived betrayal of Ukraine, officials enriching themselves, data‑center expansion, and interventions by billionaires like Elon Musk all motivated voters to cast anti‑Trump ballots.
In his final month of campaigning, Trump held 21 rallies in 21 days, spouting odd topics, dismissing voters’ concerns about housing affordability, and was accused of deepening voter alienation.

Although Trump tried to blame everything on external factors, he privately told the New York Times that he is "absolutely willing" to accept the election results. The vote not only reshaped the power dynamics in Washington but also served as a clear reckoning by American voters of the Trump era.
